record_definition: A biological process that maintains life in an organism.
candidate_definition: A cellular process consisting of the biochemical pathways by which a living organism transforms chemical substances. This includes including anabolism (biosynthetic process) and catabolism (catabolic process). Metabolic processes includes the transformation of small molecules, as well  macromolecular processes such as DNA repair and replication, protein synthesis and degradation.
review_rationale: Definitions agree on organismal biochemical metabolism; the TraitRecord label is a declared GO exact synonym.

record_definition: A characteristic of an entity that depends on the entity's existence, size, color, and physiological traits.
candidate_definition: A dependent entity that inheres in a bearer by virtue of how the bearer is related to other entities
review_rationale: Both terms denote a specifically dependent quality inhering in a bearer.

record_definition: A material entity that is a physical entity of interest in chemistry, including molecular entities, parts thereof, and chemical substances. Used as the range class for the majority of METPO chemical-use OBJECT_PROPERTYs (uses_as_carbon_source, uses_as_electron_donor, ferments, oxidizes, etc.) so that organism-to-chemical assertions resolve to a curated chemical class.
candidate_definition: A chemical entity is a physical entity of interest in chemistry including molecular entities, parts thereof, and chemical substances.
review_rationale: Existing xref; both terms denote the upper class of entities of chemical interest.

record_definition: An oxygen preference in which growth occurs in the presence of molecular oxygen (O₂), typically using O₂ as the terminal electron acceptor.
candidate_definition: A quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's dependence on oxygen.
review_rationale: Both denote oxygen-dependent growth/aerobic quality.

record_definition: An oxygen preference in which growth occurs in the absence of molecular oxygen (O₂).
candidate_definition: A quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's independence on oxygen.
review_rationale: Both denote oxygen-independent growth/anaerobic quality.

record_definition: A execution of a genetically-encoded biological module or program. It consists of all the steps required to achieve the specific biological objective of the module. A biological process is accomplished by a particular set of molecular functions carried out by specific gene products (or macromolecular complexes), often in a highly regulated manner and in a particular temporal sequence.
candidate_definition: A biological process is the execution of a genetically-encoded biological module or program. It consists of all the steps required to achieve the specific biological objective of the module. A biological process is accomplished by a particular set of molecular functions carried out by specific gene products (or macromolecular complexes), often in a highly regulated manner and in a particular temporal sequence.
review_rationale: Existing xref; the TraitRecord label is a declared GO exact synonym and the definitions agree on biological process.

record_definition: A cell shape in which an organism forms circular or toroidal structures.
candidate_definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having a shape like a ring (a circular shape enclosing a space).
review_rationale: Both definitions denote a circular or toroidal ring shape.

record_definition: A cell shape in which an organism has multiple radiating projections from a central body.
candidate_definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being arranged like rays or radii; radiating from a common center.
review_rationale: Both definitions denote radiating projections from a common center.

record_definition: A respiration in which molecular oxygen serves as the terminal electron acceptor in the electron transport chain, generating ATP through oxidative phosphorylation with water as the final product.
candidate_definition: The enzymatic release of energy from inorganic and organic compounds (especially carbohydrates and fats) which requires oxygen as the terminal electron acceptor.
review_rationale: Both define respiration using oxygen as terminal electron acceptor.

record_definition: A respiration in which an organism uses electron acceptors other than oxygen for energy production.
candidate_definition: The enzymatic release of energy from inorganic and organic compounds (especially carbohydrates and fats) which uses compounds other than oxygen (e.g. nitrate, sulfate) as the terminal electron acceptor.
review_rationale: Both define respiration using a terminal electron acceptor other than oxygen.

record_definition: A metabolism that generates ATP through the transfer of electrons from electron donors to electron acceptors via redox reactions, coupled to the pumping of protons across a membrane to create an electrochemical gradient.
candidate_definition: The phosphorylation of ADP to ATP that accompanies the oxidation of a metabolite through the operation of the respiratory chain. Oxidation of compounds establishes a proton gradient across the membrane, providing the energy for ATP synthesis.
review_rationale: Both define respiratory-chain oxidation coupled to ADP phosphorylation through a proton gradient.

record_definition: A metabolism in which electrons are transferred from an electron donor to an electron acceptor.
candidate_definition: A process in which a series of electron carriers operate together to transfer electrons from donors such as NADH and FADH2 to any of several different terminal electron acceptors to generate a transmembrane electrochemical gradient.
review_rationale: The TraitRecord permits any donor-to-acceptor electron transfer; GO requires a respiratory carrier chain that generates a transmembrane electrochemical gradient.

record_definition: A metabolism in which methane is produced as the primary end product through the reduction of carbon-containing compounds, formate, methanol, or acetate, exclusively performed by methanogenic archaea under strictly anaerobic conditions.
candidate_definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of methane, a colorless, odorless, flammable gas with the formula CH4. It is the simplest of the alkanes.
review_rationale: Both define the reactions and pathways that form methane.

record_definition: A phenotype that is relating to an organism's ability to form dormant, stress-resistant endospores.
candidate_definition: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of a spore over time, from its initiation to the mature structure. A spore is a structure that can be used for dissemination, for survival of adverse conditions because of its heat and desiccation resistance, and/or for reproduction.
review_rationale: The TraitRecord is restricted to dormant stress-resistant endospores; GO covers development of spores generally.

record_definition: A respiration that generates energy through the oxidation of organic compounds without using an external electron acceptor, using organic molecules as both electron donors and final electron acceptors.
candidate_definition: The metabolic process that uses oxidation-reduction reactions of organic compounds and substrate-level phosphorylation for the generation of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), without consuming oxygen and is independent of electron transport chains.
review_rationale: Both define oxygen-independent organic redox metabolism with substrate-level phosphorylation.

record_definition: A pH growth preference in which an organism grows optimally at pH values below 5.
candidate_definition: An affinity inhering in an anatomical structure by virtue of the bearer exhibiting a molecular interaction for acidic dyes under specific pH conditions.
review_rationale: PATO denotes affinity for acidic histological dyes, not microbial growth at low environmental pH.

record_definition: A phenotype characterized by the color of pigments produced by a microorganism.
candidate_definition: The accumulation of pigment in an organism, tissue or cell, either by increased deposition or by increased number of cells.
review_rationale: The TraitRecord is a color phenotype; GO denotes the biological process of pigment accumulation.

candidate_definition: a relation between an independent continuant (the bearer) and a quality, in which the quality specifically depends on the bearer for its existence
review_rationale: Both are the bearer-to-dependent-quality relation.

candidate_definition: A relationship that holds between a biological entity and a phenotype. Here a phenotype is construed broadly as any kind of quality of an organism part, a collection of these qualities, or a change in quality or qualities (e.g. abnormally increased temperature). The subject of this relationship can be an organism (where the organism has the phenotype, i.e. the qualities inhere in parts of this organism), a genomic entity such as a gene or genotype (if modifications of the gene or the genotype causes the phenotype), or a condition such as a disease (such that if the condition inheres in an organism, then the organism has the phenotype).
review_rationale: Both are the biological-entity-to-phenotype relation.

record_definition: A general OBJECT_PROPERTY relating an organism to a biological process or metabolic capability the organism is capable of. Intended use is predicate + class composition at assertion time, with a METPO biological-process (or GO biological-process) class as the object.
candidate_definition: A relation between a material entity (such as a cell) and a process, in which the material entity has the ability to carry out the process.
review_rationale: Existing xref; both denote the relation between a bearer and a biological process it is capable of carrying out.

record_definition: An OBJECT_PROPERTY relating an organism to a chemical that the organism produces and exports or accumulates as a metabolic product.
candidate_definition: a produces b if some process that occurs_in a has_output b, where a and b are material entities. Examples: hybridoma cell line produces monoclonal antibody reagent; chondroblast produces avascular GAG-rich matrix.
review_rationale: Existing xref; both denote production of an output, and the labels are canonical on both terms.

record_definition: An OBJECT_PROPERTY relating an organism to a chemical that the organism transports across its membranes (without specifying direction or coupling).
candidate_definition: Holds between p and c when p is a transport process or transporter activity and the outcome of this p is to move c from one location to another.
review_rationale: METPO relates an organism to a transported chemical; RO relates a transport process or activity to its cargo.

record_definition: An OBJECT_PROPERTY relating an organism to a chemical that the organism imports from the extracellular environment into the cytoplasm.
candidate_definition: Holds between p and c when p is a transportation or localization process and the outcome of this process is to move c to a destination that is part of some s, where the start location of c is part of the region that surrounds s.
review_rationale: METPO relates an organism to a chemical; RO imports has a transportation/localization process as subject.

record_definition: An OBJECT_PROPERTY relating an organism to a chemical that the organism exports from the cytoplasm to the periplasm or extracellular environment.
candidate_definition: Holds between p and c when p is a transportation or localization process and the outcome of this process is to move c to a destination that is part of some s, where the end location of c is part of the region that surrounds s.
review_rationale: METPO relates an organism to a chemical; RO exports has a transportation/localization process as subject.

record_definition: A metabolic process in which an organism assimilates inorganic carbon (CO2 or bicarbonate) into organic compounds (autotrophy). Six distinct natural autotrophic carbon-fixation pathways are currently recognized.
candidate_definition: A metabolic process in which carbon (usually derived from carbon dioxide) is incorporated into organic compounds (usually carbohydrates).
candidate_exact_synonyms: autotrophic CO2 fixation | autotrophic CO2 fixation pathway | autotrophy
review_rationale: Both define assimilation of inorganic carbon into organic compounds.

record_definition: An autotrophic carbon-fixation pathway (reductive citric acid / Arnon-Buchanan cycle) that runs the tricarboxylic acid cycle in reverse to fix CO2. It operates in anaerobic and microaerophilic bacteria such as green sulfur bacteria (Chlorobium) and Aquificales.
candidate_definition: A pathway leading to the fixation of two molecules of CO2 and the production of one molecule of acetyl-CoA; essentially the oxidative TCA cycle running in reverse. Acetyl-CoA is reductively carboxylated to pyruvate, from which all other central metabolites can be formed. Most of the enzymes of reductive and oxidative TCA cycle are shared, with the exception of three key enzymes that allow the cycle to run in reverse: ATP citrate lyase, 2-oxoglutarate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase, and fumarate reductase. 2-oxoglutarate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase catalyzes the carboxylation of succinyl-CoA to 2-oxoglutarate, ATP citrate lyase the ATP-dependent cleavage of citrate to acetyl-CoA and oxaloacetate, and fumarate reductase the reduction of fumarate forming succinate.
candidate_exact_synonyms: reductive carboxylate cycle | reductive carboxylic acid cycle | reductive citric acid pathway | reductive Kreb's cycle | reductive TCA cycle
review_rationale: Both define the reverse TCA carbon-fixation pathway producing acetyl-CoA.

record_definition: A fermentation in which pyruvate is decarboxylated to acetaldehyde (releasing CO2) and then reduced by NADH to ethanol, regenerating NAD+ for glycolysis. Characteristic of yeasts and the bacterium Zymomonas mobilis.
candidate_definition: The anaerobic chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of pyruvate into ethanol and carbon dioxide (CO2).
candidate_exact_synonyms: ethanol fermentation | glucose fermentation to ethanol
review_rationale: Both define pyruvate fermentation to ethanol and carbon dioxide.

record_definition: A phototrophic metabolism that uses light energy and chlorophyll- or bacteriochlorophyll-based photochemical reaction centers to drive electron flow, fixing CO2 and/or generating reducing power. Subdivided into oxygenic and anoxygenic photosynthesis.
candidate_definition: The synthesis by organisms of organic chemical compounds, especially carbohydrates, from carbon dioxide (CO2) using energy obtained from light rather than from the oxidation of chemical compounds.
review_rationale: Both define light-powered synthesis/fixation of organic compounds.

record_definition: An ecological lifestyle in which cells form surface-attached, matrix-enclosed multicellular communities (biofilms) held together by extracellular polymeric substances — a widespread mode of microbial life.
candidate_definition: A process in which planktonically growing microorganisms grow at a liquid-air interface or on a solid substrate under the flow of a liquid and produce extracellular polymers that facilitate matrix formation, resulting in a change in the organisms' growth rate and gene transcription.
review_rationale: The TraitRecord denotes the ecological biofilm lifestyle; GO denotes the process that forms the biofilm.

record_definition: A morphology trait in which the cell is surrounded by a well-organized layer of polysaccharide (or rarely polypeptide) external to the cell envelope, mediating adhesion, desiccation resistance, and immune evasion.
candidate_definition: A protective structure surrounding some fungi and bacteria, attached externally to the cell wall and composed primarily of polysaccharides. Capsules are highly organized structures that adhere strongly to cells and cannot be easily removed. Capsules play important roles in pathogenicity, preventing phagocytosis by other cells, adherence, and resistance to desiccation.
review_rationale: Both define the organized protective extracellular capsule of bacteria or fungi.

record_definition: A morphology trait in which the cell surface is coated by a crystalline, two-dimensional array of self-assembling proteinaceous (glyco)protein subunits (a surface layer), found in many bacteria and most archaea.
candidate_definition: A crystalline protein layer surrounding some bacteria.
review_rationale: The TraitRecord explicitly includes archaeal S-layers; the GO definition is restricted to bacteria.

record_definition: An intracellular storage inclusion composed of polyhydroxyalkanoate (e.g. polyhydroxybutyrate, PHB), a carbon and energy reserve accumulated as cytoplasmic granules.
candidate_definition: An inclusion body located in the cytoplasm of prokaryotes that consists of polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) molecules and associated proteins, surrounded by a phospholipid monolayer; the proteins include PHA synthase, PHA depolymerase and 3HB-oligomer hydroxylase, phasins (PhaPs), which are thought to be the major structural proteins of the membrane surrounding the inclusion, and the regulator of phasin expression PhaR.
review_rationale: Both define a cytoplasmic polyhydroxyalkanoate storage granule.

record_definition: An intracellular gas-filled proteinaceous inclusion that provides buoyancy, allowing planktonic bacteria and archaea to position themselves in the water column.
candidate_definition: An intracellular non-membrane-bounded organelle; a hollow structure made of protein, which usually has the form of a cylindrical tube closed by conical end caps. By regulating their relative gas vesicle content, aquatic microbes are able to perform vertical migrations.
review_rationale: Both define the proteinaceous gas-filled buoyancy organelle.

record_definition: A membrane-bounded intracellular organelle containing a magnetic iron-mineral crystal (magnetite or greigite); chains of magnetosomes allow magnetotactic bacteria to align with and navigate along geomagnetic field lines.
candidate_definition: A membrane-bound organelle that envelops particles of magnetic iron minerals in magnetotactic bacteria. Magnetosomes form linear chains that align along the cellular motility axis at midcell and function in bacterial navigation along the Earth's magnetic field. They are formed by invagination of the cell inner membrane; in some species they remain connected to the inner membrane, in others they pinch off to form independent intracellular vesicles.
review_rationale: Both define the membrane-bound magnetic-mineral organelle of magnetotactic bacteria.

record_definition: A bacterial microcompartment — a polyhedral protein-shelled organelle that encapsulates RuBisCO and carbonic anhydrase to concentrate CO2 for carbon fixation in cyanobacteria and many chemoautotrophs.
candidate_definition: An organelle consisting of a proteinaceous coat and enzymes for the fixation of CO2. It augments the concentration of CO2 in the vicinity of RuBisCO to increase the efficiency of CO2 fixation under atmospheric conditions.
review_rationale: Both define the protein-shelled carbon-fixation microcompartment containing RuBisCO.

record_definition: A physiological enzyme-activity phenotype in which a cell produces catalase, which decomposes hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen; it is the basis of the diagnostic catalase test.
candidate_definition: Catalysis of the reaction: 2 H2O2 = O2 + 2 H2O.
review_rationale: The TraitRecord denotes the cell-level catalase-positive phenotype; GO denotes the molecular catalytic activity.

record_definition: A physiological enzyme-activity phenotype in which a cell produces urease, which hydrolyzes urea to ammonia and carbon dioxide, typically raising local pH; it is the basis of the diagnostic urease test.
candidate_definition: Catalysis of the reaction: urea + 2 H2O + H+ = hydrogencarbonate + 2 NH4+.
review_rationale: The TraitRecord denotes the cell-level urease-positive phenotype; GO denotes the molecular catalytic activity.

record_definition: The physiological process by which a dormant spore exits dormancy and resumes vegetative growth in response to germinant signals, including release of dipicolinic acid and rehydration of the spore core.
candidate_definition: The physiological and developmental changes that occur in a spore following release from dormancy up to the earliest signs of growth (e.g. emergence from a spore wall).
review_rationale: Both define exit from spore dormancy through the earliest resumption of growth.

record_definition: A cell-density-dependent regulatory physiology in which cells produce, release, and detect diffusible autoinducer signals to coordinate gene expression across a population.
candidate_definition: The cell-cell signaling process in which single-celled organisms carry out coordinated responses by monitoring their own population density, and often also that of other microbes, by producing small, diffusible, signal molecules, detecting the concentration of these molecules, and triggering a signal transduction pathway when a certain threshold is reached. Quorum sensing can occur amongst microbial communities in the environment or within host organisms.
review_rationale: Both define density-dependent diffusible cell-cell signaling and coordinated response.

record_definition: A physiological capability to emit visible light through a luciferase-catalyzed reaction, frequently regulated by quorum sensing in marine bacteria such as Aliivibrio and Photobacterium.
candidate_definition: The production of light by certain enzyme-catalyzed reactions in cells.
review_rationale: The TraitRecord denotes a cell-level capability; GO denotes the light-producing biological process.

record_definition: A behavioral physiology in which cells bias their movement toward attractants or away from repellents by modulating flagellar motor switching in response to chemical gradients.
candidate_definition: The directed movement of a motile cell or organism, or the directed growth of a cell guided by a specific chemical concentration gradient. Movement may be towards a higher concentration (positive chemotaxis) or towards a lower concentration (negative chemotaxis).
candidate_exact_synonyms: taxis in response to chemical stimulus
review_rationale: Both define directed movement along a chemical concentration gradient.

record_definition: A genomics trait describing possession of a CRISPR-Cas adaptive immune system that records fragments of invading nucleic acids in CRISPR arrays and uses Cas proteins to recognize and cleave matching sequences.
candidate_definition: A defense response of that serves to clear host cells of foreign DNA and RNA. It has three distinct stage: acquisition of foreign DNA by integration into CRISPR loci in the host chromosome, CRISPR RNA (crRNA) biogenesis, and target interference. CRISPR stands for Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeat, which describes the nature of the loci.
review_rationale: The TraitRecord denotes possession of the CRISPR-Cas system; GO denotes the defense response carried out by it.

record_definition: A genomics trait describing the number of complete genome copies per cell; many bacteria and archaea are polyploid, maintaining many chromosome copies that support survival, repair, and large cell size.
candidate_definition: A cellular quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's number of homologous sets of chromosomes in the nucleus or primary chromosome-containing compartment of the cell, each set essentially coding for all the biological traits of the organism.
review_rationale: Both define the number of complete homologous chromosome/genome sets in a cell.

record_definition: A metabolism in which an organism reduces atmospheric dinitrogen (N2) to ammonia using the nitrogenase enzyme complex, making fixed nitrogen biologically available (diazotrophy).
candidate_definition: The process in which nitrogen is taken from its relatively inert molecular form (N2) in the atmosphere and converted into ammonium, which is more biologically available.
review_rationale: Both define conversion of atmospheric dinitrogen to biologically available ammonium.

record_definition: An anaerobic respiratory metabolism in which an organism uses sulfate as the terminal electron acceptor, reducing it to hydrogen sulfide while oxidizing organic matter or hydrogen for energy.
candidate_definition: The reduction of sulfate to hydrogen sulfide, which acts as a terminal electron acceptor. Sulfate is activated to adenosine-phosphosulfate (APS) which is then reduced to sulfite, which is in turn reduced to hydrogen sulfide.
review_rationale: Both define sulfate reduction to hydrogen sulfide as terminal-electron-acceptor respiration.

record_definition: A metabolism in which an organism oxidizes reduced inorganic sulfur compounds (sulfide, elemental sulfur, thiosulfate) to sulfate, conserving energy and often supporting chemolithotrophic growth.
candidate_definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting the addition of oxygen to elemental sulfur.
review_rationale: The TraitRecord covers oxidation of sulfide, elemental sulfur, and thiosulfate; GO is restricted to adding oxygen to elemental sulfur.

record_definition: A biopolymer-degradation metabolism in which an organism hydrolyzes xylan, the most abundant hemicellulose, into xylose and xylo-oligosaccharides using xylanases and accessory enzymes.
candidate_definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of xylan, a polymer containing a beta-1,4-linked D-xylose backbone.
candidate_exact_synonyms: xylan breakdown | xylan catabolism | xylan degradation
review_rationale: Both define enzymatic breakdown of xylan.

record_definition: A biopolymer-degradation metabolism in which an organism breaks down lignin, the recalcitrant aromatic heteropolymer of plant cell walls, using oxidative enzymes such as peroxidases and laccases.
candidate_definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of lignins, a class of polymers of phenylpropanoid units.
candidate_exact_synonyms: lignin breakdown | lignin catabolism | lignin degradation
review_rationale: Both define breakdown of lignin polymers.

record_definition: A biopolymer-degradation metabolism in which an organism hydrolyzes starch (amylose and amylopectin) to maltooligosaccharides and glucose using amylases and related glycoside hydrolases.
candidate_definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of starch, the most important reserve polysaccharide in plants.
candidate_exact_synonyms: starch breakdown | starch catabolism | starch degradation
review_rationale: Both define breakdown of starch polymers.

record_definition: A biopolymer-degradation metabolism in which an organism secretes proteases to hydrolyze extracellular proteins and peptides into amino acids and short peptides for nutrition.
candidate_definition: The hydrolysis of proteins into smaller polypeptides and/or amino acids by cleavage of their peptide bonds.
review_rationale: The TraitRecord is restricted to secreted nutritional proteolysis; GO covers all protein hydrolysis.
